Visit note | 2025-05-25 04:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Shapla Hasan, 58, female. Mrs. Hasan comes in for review reporting a racing heart, shaky hands, and a strong intolerance to heat. She mentions that these symptoms began after a stressful family event in Bogura. She works as a textile engineer. She has no chronic comorbidities. On examination, pulse is noted at 120 bpm, BP 112/70 mmHg, and weight 92 kg. Heart sounds are bounding and fine tremors are visible in both outstretched hands. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice given to avoid excess tea and coffee and to rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-05-25 04:30 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Jui Miah, 52, female. Mrs. Miah presents for her first visit complaining of pain behind her eyes and a faint rash appearing on her arms. She reports this started after a neighbour in Tejgaon was admitted with dengue. Her occupation is a tailor. She has no known comorbidities. On examination, her temperature is 101.0°F, platelet count is 102000 per microlitre, BP 127/84 mmHg, pulse 107 bpm, and weight 95 kg. She appears flushed with mild retro-orbital tenderness. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.
